Thanks for looping me in. Hi Sara — sorry for the confusion and thanks for sending the invoice. A couple of notes from the account side:

- We do issue self-serve trial credits automatically for PLG signups, but in some cases (depending on billing address / VAT reg) the system will still create an invoice with tax lines even if we later apply a promotional credit. That can look like a charge until the credit is applied.
- If you can provide a PO number and confirm the company address (EU VAT or US), we can expedite a credit note and a 14-day trial extension while AP processes paperwork.

I’ve asked Rishi to confirm whether this invoice already has a pending credit in our system or whether we need to issue a manual reversal/credit note. If we do a manual credit, we’ll include a small explanatory note for your AP team about how promotional credits and VAT are handled.

Lauren Bishop | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.example
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.example>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@brightlayer.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected token charges on invoice after trial

Hi team — I pulled the billing record for BrightLayer (request traced to DL-9876). Summary and next steps: 

1) What happened: The self-serve signup did correctly assign a $1,000 promotional credit to the account. However, the billing system created an invoice for token usage dated 2027-10-01 and, because the billing address on file included a UK/EU VAT indicator, a VAT line was added at the time the invoice was generated. The promo credit is applied at invoice settlement time; until we issue a credit note it will appear as a net charge.

2) Why VAT shows: Tax is calculated on the taxable base before promotional credits in our current accounting flow. For promo credits tied to marketing/test usage (not a discount on a PO), tax may still appear on the invoice depending on the jurisdiction.

3) Recommended fix: We can issue a manual credit note that reverses the invoice (credit for token usage + VAT reversal) and post it with a short explanation for AP. Additionally, we can add a $1,000 trial extension to ensure your engineering team has uninterrupted tooling while AP completes your PO.

Required from BrightLayer to proceed:
- Confirm PO number (if AP requires it) or confirm they will accept credit note without PO.
- Confirm billing address / VAT id (if EU).

Operational timeline:
- If we get PO / billing confirmation by EOD tomorrow, finance can generate the credit note within 48 hours and we’ll attach the explanatory statement for your records.
- Trial extension and account flags will be applied same-day when finance creates the credit.

I will create the credit note draft and share it internally for sign-off; Marissa/Lauren, please let me know if there are customer-specific copy/snippets AP expects.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Finance Manager, Billing Ops | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.example

Hi Sara / AP team — quick update and next steps from our side. Per Rishi: the promo credit is on the account but we need a small administrative step to get a formal credit note issued that reverses the invoice and the VAT.

What we need from BrightLayer (one of the two):
- PO number to reference on the credit note; OR
- Confirmation that AP will accept a credit note referencing your company name and invoice number without a PO.

If you can reply with either option today, I’ll get Rishi to generate the credit note and attach an explanation for your records. Also attaching a temporary credit memo/placeholder for AP while we finalize the formal document.

Attached: credit_note_brightlayer_20271008.pdf (PDF, 5 KB) — draft placeholder

We’ll also add a 14-day trial extension to the account when the credit is posted so your engineers aren’t blocked. If you need a DocuSign or a PO-stamped copy, let me know and I’ll route it through our finance ops (we can include the HubSpot company id: 67890 on the credit note).

Best,
